options.O1: Fixed core of built-in fields + an extensible attribute system
options.O2: Everything is an attribute (only identity/structure stays outside)
options.O3: Large built-in core + a capped set of custom fields

unanimous: 13 of 13 keep a fixed core of identity + structure outside the extensible system — nobody puts everything in the bag. 8 of 13 keep definition and value as separate objects (3 partial: Amazon, eBay, WooCommerce; 2 no: Google, Walmart — both flat feeds).

rows.h: write path; the read model would file O1
rows.shape: Seven property groups on the product-type definition (product_identity verified on the first-party reference 2026-09-21: propertyNames [item_name, brand, external_product_id, gtin_exemption_reason, merchant_suggested_asin, product_type, product_category, product_subcategory, item_type_keyword]; requirements ∈ {LISTING, LISTING_PRODUCT_ONLY, LISTING_OFFER_ONLY}, requirementsEnforced ∈ {ENFORCED, NOT_ENFORCED}) — offer · images · shipping · variations · safety_and_compliance · product_identity · product_details — so price (list_price), images, weight and the title are all properties of the type schema; item_name, brand, product_description sit in PET_FOOD's root required. Outside the bag: sku (a URL path parameter, never a schema attribute). The read side projects scalars beside the bag (ItemSummaryByMarketplace.brand/.itemName/.manufacturer/.color/.size/.style) plus first-class identifiers, images, dimensions, classifications, relationships. The bag is declared open: "ItemAttributes": {…"additionalProperties": true}. Definition = Attribute (name PK) + ProductTypeAttribute join carrying marketplaceId, parentageLevel, requiredness — requiredness is a property of the join; JSON-side type/constraints/enum UNKNOWN. 2,336 distinct attribute names; 213 types → 208 distinct attributes, 1,154 pairs, 107 used by exactly one type. Brand: an attribute and a read scalar and a search refinement; a family's “non-varying attributes” (brand, model name, style) must match across children.

Product 83 fields, ProductVariant 52. Built-in: title, handle, descriptionHtml, productType (free text), vendor, tags, category, options, price, compareAtPrice, sku, barcode, inventoryItem. No weight on ProductVariant: it hangs off inventoryItem.measurement.weight {unit: WeightUnit!, value: Float!} (REST still shows grams/weight/weight_unit). Length/width/height not answered. Extension = MetafieldDefinition (17 fields; owner types incl. PRODUCT and PRODUCTVARIANT); 48 basic + 12 reference + 53 list types, and “the value is always entered and stored as a string, regardless of type”; a value may exist with definition: null. Second definition surface: the taxonomy — 8,240 base + 316 extended attributes, 93,007 category→attribute edges, 74,820 values; flavor on 293 categories. Brand: vendor: String!, free text, no validation; the word “brand” occurs zero times in the record.

rows.h: no definition object at all; no per-category schema
rows.shape: One global flat set: 145 properties on Merchant API products_v1 (95 on v1beta, 104 on Content API v2.1; 85 in the human spec). Every fact is a flat property: title, description, price, gtins, brand (Max 70 chars, required except movies/books/music), productWeight, productLength/Height/Width, shippingWeight, googleProductCategory, productTypes, color, size, material, pattern, itemGroupId, variantOptions, productDetails. Four open merchant-named bags beside them: customAttributes (≤2,500, 102.4 kB total, recursive), productDetails (≤100; suggested keys incl. Scent, Flavor), cloudExportAdditionalProperties, variantOptions. The 145 names are the schema; the bags are {name, value} with no definition. Category gates requiredness, and in one case existence (subscription_cost: “approved product categories only”).

Inventory API Product built-ins: brand, ean, epid, isbn, mpn, upc (every identifier is variant-level) + title, description, imageUrls, subtitle, videoIds, and aspects. Price/quantity on the Offer. Extension = the aspect, owned by the leaf category: 197,046 aspects over 15,111 leaves; “Each category has a different set of aspects and different requirements for aspect values.” The aspect has no id: an item's values are aspects = {name: [strings]} (Trading: NameValueListArrayType). Definition = AspectConstraint, exactly 11 properties, identified only by localizedAspectName within a category. Caps: name 40 chars, value 50, 30 values per multi-value aspect. Brand: built-in field and aspect; catalog-matched (ePID/GTIN) aspects are auto-filled and “Sellers cannot change the value of aspects that are based on a catalog product.”

rows.h: the cleanest published instance of the line
rows.shape: Two fixed blocks, nothing else: MPItem {Visible, Orderable}, additionalProperties: false. Orderable = 23 properties, required sku, productIdentifiers, price, ShippingWeight, country_of_origin_substantial_transformation (+ inventory, msrp, product_package_dimensions_and_weight, fulfillmentLagTime, …). Visible = the per-product-type attribute set where merchandising facts live: productName, brand, shortDescription, mainImageUrl, netContent, flavor are type slots (required for Toothpastes). 6,967 types · 383,947 slots · 6,576 distinct names · 28–183 per type. No definition object on the write path: $ref 0, $id 0, valueId 0 over 451 MB — every attribute written out in full per type, so color has 126 distinct definitions, size 438, flavor 50. Governance is a description prefix: "Closed List - …" (has enum) · "Alphanumeric, N characters - …" · "Number, Value range: A to B - …" · "Decimal, …". No cap.

Item fixed fields: item_name REQ, description REQ, original_price REQ, weight REQ, item_sku, has_model, condition, gtin_code, brand {brand_id int32 REQ, original_brand_name string REQ}, dimension {package_height/length/width}, logistic_info REQ, seller_stock, price_info … plus attribute_list. Definition object with shared value rows: get_attribute_tree(category_id) → attribute_id, name, mandatory, attribute_value_list[{value_id, name, value_unit, child_attribute_list}], attribute_info {input_type (5), input_validation_type (5), format_type (2), date_format_type, attribute_unit_list, max_value_count, is_oem, support_search_value}; “only last-level categories can retrieve attribute data.” A typed value carries a unit (name = “5kg”, value_unit = the unit); axis labels do not. Brand: a reference to a platform-owned brand entity (brand_id). No documented cap.

Era A (terminated 2025-09-30): fixed columns name ≤70, category_id, price, status, stock, min_order, weight, weight_unit, condition, sku ≤50, description ≤2000, dimension, annotations []string, etalase, variant; extension = the Annotation (“product specification based on category ID”), group = a bare variant string name with no id, sort_order, values[{id, name, data}]. No brand or GTIN field in the create body. Era B: 34 depth-0 fields incl. title, description, category_id, brand_id, main_images, package_dimensions, package_weight, product_attributes, certifications, size_chart; price, inventory and identifiers are SKU-level (skus.price, skus.inventory, skus.identifier_code with GTIN|EAN|UPC|ISBN|JAN). Definition: GET /product/202309/categories/{id}/attributes → id, name, type, is_requried [sic], values[{id, name, icon_url}], value_data_format, is_customizable, requirement_conditions, is_multiple_selection. Vendor's own split: product attributes (manufacturer, origin, materials) vs sales attributes (“specific to the variant (aka SKU) such as size, color, length”). Brand: platform-owned Brand entity (brand_id; “Brand does not exist” error).

rows.h: the cap's scope (account vs app_id) unresolved by the vendor's own artifacts
rows.shape: CatalogItem = 27 properties enumerated whole (name, description_html, categories, item_options, variations, product_type, is_alcoholic, food_and_beverage_details, kitchen_name, …). Price, SKU, UPC on the variation: price_money, sku, upc, measurement_unit_id. Extension: 10 seller-visible + 10 seller-hidden custom attributes — live-verified: the 11th SELLER_VISIBILITY_READ_WRITE_VALUES definition → HTTP 400 ITEMS_CUSTOM_ATTRIBUTE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (“for app_id … exceeded limit of 10”). Definition = CatalogCustomAttributeDefinition (12 properties; required type, name, allowed_object_types; key immutable; type ∈ STRING|BOOLEAN|NUMBER|SELECTION). Value = CatalogObject.custom_attribute_values, a map keyed by the definition's key landing in string_value / number_value / boolean_value / selection_uid_values — inline, not a shared row. Weight: not a product field; the variation points at a CatalogMeasurementUnit. Brand: not answered (only "cocoa_brand" as a key example).

One Product row for every role. catalog.xsd complexType.Product opens with ean, upc, unit, unit-quantity (xsd:decimal), unit-measure (String.60), then classification-category, variations, images, product-set-products, bundled-products, custom-attributes. Three-level definition: ObjectTypeDefinition → ObjectAttributeGroup → ObjectAttributeDefinition with unit: String (“inches for length or pounds for weight”) and valueTypeCode (18 constants: INT NUMBER STRING TEXT HTML DATE IMAGE BOOLEAN MONEY QUANTITY DATETIME EMAIL PASSWORD SET_OF_STRING SET_OF_INT SET_OF_NUMBER ENUM_OF_STRING ENUM_OF_INT) vs the XSD's 16 (no MONEY/QUANTITY — the two disagree). System/custom switch: @system: xsd:boolean default="false" on the attribute reference; REST prefixes custom attributes c_. Brand: zero occurrences in the record.

Non-attribute columns on pim_catalog_product, whole: uuid, id, identifier, enabled, raw_values, created, updated, rawQuantifiedAssociations + edges family, parent, familyVariant, groups, categories. Everything describing content is an attribute; 19 CE types incl. pim_catalog_identifier, pim_catalog_price_collection, pim_catalog_image, pim_catalog_metric. Title = an attribute the family nominates (attributeAsLabel = name); price = price_collection; weight = metric, typed: {"amount":"800.0000","unit":"GRAM","symbol":"g"}; barcode = no such concept (0 files over 17.5 MB). Definition = pim_catalog_attribute (~30 columns: is_required, is_unique, is_localizable, is_scopable, sortOrder, useableAsGridFilter, metricFamily, defaultMetricUnit; type immutable). Values in raw_values JSON as {locale, scope, data}; option values are shared AttributeOption rows but the product copies the code string (“referential integrity is a validator, not a foreign key”). The Family decides the attribute set, never the category (0 hits over 344 files). Brand: ships both — a pim_catalog_simpleselect attribute in the demo catalogue and (EE) a Reference Entity, with the stated trigger: “its own attributes (a label, a logo, a description or photos) … dedicated pages on one's e-commerce website”.

No tables of its own: products, variations, categories, types and attribute values are WordPress rows (wp_posts, wp_terms, wp_term_taxonomy, wp_term_relationships, wp_postmeta) + two WooCommerce tables: woocommerce_attribute_taxonomies (the global registry) and wc_product_attributes_lookup (a filter index). post_title = title; _sku, _global_unique_id (GTIN), _price = postmeta. Three attribute objects: (1) per-product WC_Product_Attribute {id, name, options, position, visible, variation} serialised into one _product_attributes postmeta row; (2) global definition, six columns attribute_id, attribute_name, attribute_label, attribute_type, attribute_orderby, attribute_public — none references a category or type; (3) the value = a WordPress term, “a bare label — six fields, none a quantity, unit or dimension”, shared across products. A product-local attribute has no definition row (id 0; is_taxonomy() { return 0 < id }). No attribute-set object (1 false-positive hit over 2,833 PHP files). Brand: product_brand is a core taxonomy since 9.4.0 (2024-11-11) — “similar to Categories”, dedicated brand pages — the one merchant-owned brand entity in the thirteen.

rows.h: thinnest core of the nine; closest to O2
rows.shape: ProductData 13 properties: name, categories, categoryOrderHints?, description?, slug, metaTitle?, metaDescription?, metaKeywords?, masterVariant, variants, searchKeywords, attributes, defaultVariant?. ProductVariant 13: id, sku?, key?, prices?, attributes?, price?, images?, assets?, availability?, … Weight is an ordinary attribute — {"name":"weight","value":250}, no unit anywhere. No barcode/GTIN field on Product or Variant. Definition = AttributeDefinition {type, name (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ 2..256), label, isRequired, attributeConstraint, inputTip?, inputHint, isSearchable, level} — “Not a resource: no id, no version; reached only through its ProductType.” Value = Attribute {name, value: any}. Closed lists live on the definition, per ProductType; the same name across types must have the same type. Brand: only vendor-authored attribute names (brand, tablet-brand). No cap per type; 50 Product + 50 Variant attributes indexable.

rows.h: one registry, two storage strategies — the model behind option 4
rows.shape: catalog_product_entity = 8 columns: entity_id, attribute_set_id, type_id, sku, has_options, required_options, created_at, updated_at. Everything else is an eav_attribute row — the default set installs 43 definitions (name, sku, description, price, weight, manufacturer, image, color, status, visibility, country_of_manufacture, …). Reconciled at source: sku is installed as 'type' => 'static' → backend_type='static', and isStatic() returns true for TYPE_STATIC or '' — so Magento has a definition row for every product fact, and backend_type says whether the value lives in an EAV table or a column. Definition = eav_attribute (17 columns incl. frontend_input, backend_type, source_model, is_user_defined, is_required, is_unique; UNIQUE (entity_type_id, attribute_code)) + overlay catalog_eav_attribute (22 columns). Value: five typed tables (varchar, int, decimal, text, datetime), UNIQUE (entity_id, attribute_id, store_id); select values are shared eav_attribute_option rows referenced by integer, labels fanned out per store view. frontend_input is the free-text-vs-closed-list switch. Brand: the installed manufacturer attribute (select, user_defined). Barcode: no vendor term (0 hits). No cap.

hedges: Amazon O2 on the write path (read model would be O1) · commercetools O1 but weight is an attribute and no GTIN field exists · Square O3 on a cap of unresolved scope (if per-application, it is O1) · WooCommerce O1 with shipping dimensions unmeasured · Google O1 but with no per-category schema at all, so option 1's second clause has no analogue.
brand: Brand sub-question, revised 2026-09-19: attribute — Amazon, Walmart, commercetools, Magento (+ Akeneo CE); built-in scalar — Shopify (vendor), Google (brand), eBay (Product.brand + a Brand aspect); platform-owned registry — Shopee (brand_id), Tokopedia Era B (brand_id); merchant-owned entity — WooCommerce (product_brand taxonomy, 9.4.0), Akeneo EE (Reference Entity); not established — Square, Salesforce.
